text: dsh-wsl-first 是 DSH 的命令执行路由插件：它向系统提示词加入按优先级排列的工具选择说明，并提供 Web 侧边栏面板。插件根据当前 agent 实际可见的工具生成提示，只提及已注册工具；默认优先 wsl，其次 bash，并将 pwsh 作为最后选择。可配置优先工具、备选项、排序及提示内容，也可在面板查看当前路由。适合希望让 DSH 优先使用 WSL 或自定义命令工具顺序的用户；需要相应命令工具已由其他插件注册。

dsh-wsl-first guides DSH command execution with a system-prompt section and web sidebar. It lists tools visible to the current agent, preferring wsl, then bash, and placing pwsh last. Configure the order and inspect routing in the panel; other plugins register the tools.
想让 DSH 在执行命令时默认先用 WSL。
DSH 能按工具优先级选择 wsl、bash 和 pwsh 吗？
让系统提示词只推荐当前 agent 实际可用的命令工具。
我想调整 DSH 调用命令行工具的首选顺序。
有没有面板能查看当前命令路由和备选工具？
Make DSH prefer WSL for command execution.
Show only command tools that the current agent can actually use.
Let me inspect the preferred and fallback shell tools in a sidebar.
dsh-wsl-first 的功能「动态系统提示词路由」：根据 agent 可见的工具生成系统提示词路由段落，按首选、备选和最后选择顺序引导命令执行；不可用的工具不会被列出。
dsh-wsl-first 的功能「可配置工具优先级」：配置首选命令工具、备选工具和最后选择工具，并可通过对应环境变量覆盖默认值。
dsh-wsl-first 的功能「路由状态侧边栏」：在侧边栏打开只读面板，查看首选工具、备选项、最后选择项以及提示段落是否启用。

dsh-wsl-first README · dsh-wsl-first：**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

Make DSH reach for WSL first on Windows.

🎯 Have WSL installed? Then use it — don't let the agent default to writing PowerShell.

dsh-wsl-first README · Why：On Windows, DSH hands the model `pwsh` as its default command tool. There's nothing wrong with that in itself, but if the machine already has WSL, that default costs you.

Models write bash more naturally than PowerShell. Their command instincts are POSIX-shaped. Forcing a switch to PowerShell means translating pipes, quoting, and paths back and forth — and every mistranslation is a retry. **Every retry is tokens burned for nothing.**

dsh-wsl-first README · Why：Output is the same story. Linux commands tend to print tight, plain text. PowerShell hands you tables and object properties by default, and the same information takes visibly more room.

Paths too. The WSL tool converts `C:\...` to `/mnt/c/...` on its own, so the model never has to think about it.

So this plugin does one small thing: it adds a section to the system prompt saying to try `wsl` first. **It grants no capability and disables no tool — it just changes the default order.**

dsh-wsl-first README · Why：That prompt text only lists tools that are actually registered. If a tool isn't installed, it won't appear there, which means the model never gets told to call something that doesn't exist. A static instruction file can't do this; it just repeats what you wrote.

dsh-wsl-first README · Features：| | |
| --- | --- |
| 🚀 Saves tokens | One less syntax translation means one less retry |
| 🐧 Built for WSL | The model writes bash, and it runs Linux-side |
| 🪟 Keeps the escape hatch | When you really need Windows-native, `pwsh` is still there |
| 🔧 Configurable | Prefer bash instead, or name only `wsl` — it's a config change |
| 🩺 Never lies | Only advertises tools that are actually registered |
| 🖥 Sidebar panel | A rail entry showing the current first choice, the fallbacks, and whether the section is publishing |

dsh-wsl-first README · Sidebar panel：The plugin contributes one rail entry (a glyph plus the `WSL first` label). It opens a read-only panel showing the routing in force:

| Panel row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Reach for first | The preferred executor (`preferred`) |
| Fall back to | The alternatives (`alternatives`, minus any duplicate of the preferred) |
| Last resort | What is explicitly discouraged (`discouraged`) |
| Prompt section | Whether the section publishes, and its `order` |

dsh-wsl-first README · Sidebar panel：The panel is read-only by design: the routing belongs to the bundle row in `cordis.patch.yml`, and a form here would give one setting two owners that can disagree. Change the file and restart the profile.

It reads the row's own override first and the inherited bundle default second — the same precedence the Host applies to that row.

dsh-wsl-first README · Sidebar panel：> **The first enable needs a DSH restart.** The Host caches its client-package verdict per Loader specifier. If a profile ever resolved a build of this package *without* a client half before resolving one with it, that negative verdict is cached too, and nothing short of a restart re-evaluates it — not a reinstall, a page refresh, or HMR. After that restart, later client-artifact edits are picked up by HMR normally.

dsh-wsl-first README · Requirements：| | |
| --- | --- |
| **DSH** | `>=0.1.7-rc.2` |
| **Required service** | `systemPrompt` — ships with every standard profile |
| **Required plugin** | [dsh-wsl-tool](https://github.com/XINY11451/dsh-wsl) — provides `wsl` / `wsl-path` / `wsl-env` / `wsl-doctor` |
| **WSL** | WSL2, at least one registered distribution, `wsl.exe` on `PATH` |
| **Platform** | Any. Windows is the motivating case; the router itself is platform-independent |

dsh-wsl-first README · Requirements：This plugin registers no tools of its own — it only routes between tools other plugins provide. Without `dsh-wsl-tool` there is no `wsl` to prefer, and the section renders empty.

dsh-wsl-first README · Install：```bash
npm install dsh-wsl-first
```

Then add it to your profile's `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": ["...", "dsh-wsl-first"]

The bundle ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the routing row process-wide — every agent preset gets the section without declaring anything. **A profile restart is required**; the loader reads its composition at startup.

If the `wsl` tool itself isn't installed yet, get that first:

dsh-wsl-first README · Install：```bash
npm install dsh-wsl-tool
```

dsh-wsl-first README · DSH version compatibility：The plugin declares **no `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependency** and imports none of their values. That's deliberate: at startup DSH runs `evaluatePluginCompatibility` over every profile bundle, and if even one peer range fails to cover the running version, **the whole bundle is skipped** — `cordis.patch.yml` never takes effect, and it looks like "installed but nothing happens". With no peer range to check, that particular failure can't happen here.
dsh-wsl-first README · DSH version compatibility：If the plugin goes quiet after a DSH major upgrade, check stderr for `skipping profile bundle` and confirm `engines.dsh` still covers your version.

dsh-wsl-first README · Toggling the plugin can report an error：Switching this plugin off, or back on, from the plugin manager can fail with one of these:

```
停用失败: dsh: profile reload requires the root Include entry
启用失败: dsh: warning: 1 entry did not activate
```

**This does not affect how the plugin works.** The routing section stays in the system prompt and the plugin keeps running — only the toggle itself does not apply, and no configuration is lost.
section: Toggling the plugin can report an error

text:
dsh-wsl-first README · Toggling the plugin can report an error：**Restart DSH** — close the app and open it again. The change takes effect at startup, and everything works normally afterwards.

The same messages can appear when toggling other plugins in the same profile.

One more thing worth knowing: editing the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` while DSH is running can strip tools from live sessions. Restart after editing that file rather than relying on live reload.
section: Toggling the plugin can report an error

text: dsh-wsl-first README · Configuration：Every field is optional and settable in a profile patch (`- id: wsl-first-routing` / `config:`) or by environment variable. **Precedence: row config > environment > built-in default.**

dsh-wsl-first README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Environment | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preferred` | `wsl` | `DSH_WSL_FIRST_PREFERRED` | The tool to try first |
| `alternatives` | `['bash']` | `DSH_WSL_FIRST_ALTERNATIVES` | Tried after the preferred one (comma-separated) |
| `discouraged` | `['pwsh']` | `DSH_WSL_FIRST_DISCOURAGED` | Pushed to last resort (comma-separated) |
| `promptPolicy` | `true` | — | Publish the section at all |
| `sectionOrder` | `3260` | — | The section's sort order |
| `sectionName` | `dsh-wsl-first:shell-routing` | — | The section's stable name |
| `extraGuidance` | `''` | — | Extra text appended to the section |
| `labels` | built-in | — | `{tool: task description}` rows for the table |
| `requirePreferred` | `false` | — | Only publish while `preferred` is visible |

dsh-wsl-first README · WSL only, nothing else：```yaml
- id: wsl-first-routing
  config:
    preferred: wsl
    alternatives: []

The section then names `wsl` alone, and doesn't appear at all where `wsl` isn't installed.

dsh-wsl-first README · Prefer bash instead：```yaml
- id: wsl-first-routing
  config:
    preferred: bash
    alternatives: []

`wsl` is only the default — the plugin is a general executor router.

dsh-wsl-first README · Two configuration rules：A tool that is both an executor and a last resort is a contradiction, and it throws rather than letting a silent winner decide. Repeating `preferred` among `alternatives` is not a contradiction — it's just redundant (it happens naturally when you point `preferred` at `bash`), so it gets de-duplicated.
dsh-wsl-first README · The rendered prompt：```markdown

dsh-wsl-first README · Shell routing: wsl first：**For every command execution, call `wsl` as the first and default tool.**

| Task | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Any command, build, git, pipeline, script, file listing, search | `wsl` |
| Windows-native only: registry, services, COM, cmdlets with no Linux equivalent | `pwsh` (last resort) |

dsh-wsl-first README · Rules：- `wsl` is the primary command executor. Reach for it first, every time.
- Use `pwsh` **only** when the task genuinely requires functionality no other available tool provides — and say why in the same reply.
- Never use `pwsh` merely because it appears first in a tool list, and never as a fallback when a `wsl` command fails: fix the command and retry there.
- Do not mix shell syntaxes. A `wsl` call contains the syntax of the shell that tool runs; each executor has its own quoting and path rules.
- `wsl` paths are Linux paths (`/mnt/c/...`). Windows paths in `command`/`workdir` are translated automatically; pass `translatePaths: false` to hand a native path to a Windows program.
```

dsh-wsl-first README · Rules：That block is the real output, read back from a live session's system prompt. Note there's **no `bash` row** in it: the profile it came from had no `bash` tool registered, so the router dropped it.

dsh-wsl-first README · What it deliberately doesn't do：**It hides nothing and disables nothing.** The point is that `wsl` gets chosen first, not that `pwsh` disappears. Hiding a tool changes what the model can do; a routing section only changes what it reaches for by default.

The hard version — removing `pwsh` from the tool list entirely — is your own profile patch:

```yaml
- id: pwsh-sandbox
  disabled: true
```

Check that row's real id in your live loader tree before relying on it; a wrong id fails silently.

dsh-wsl-first README · Project layout：```
dsh-wsl-first
├── index.js          # Host half: registers the systemPrompt section
├── endpoint.js       # Client half: the sidebar panel and its rail entry
├── lib/

dsh-wsl-first README · Tests：```bash
npm test
```

Both modules under `lib/` are pure, so the tests need no DSH host. `mount.mjs` runs the real `apply` from `index.js` against a fake cordis context and asserts the registered section's name, order and rendered text. `docs.mjs` re-renders the section and compares it byte for byte against the block quoted in each README, so the documented output cannot drift from what the code emits.
